 BREAKING NEWS Nov. 13, 2026, 9:09 PM UTC U.S. news U.S. news Ground stop ordered for all airports nationwide for ‘reasons of safety’
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was “no indication as of yet” that there was anything “nefarious” behind the ground stop, but that it was a telecommunications outage. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google By Corky Siemaszko The Federal Aviation Administration on Friday ordered a nationwide ground stop on all departing flights “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.”
 The unusual alert contained no other information beyond stating that “all departing traffic should remain ground stopped until further notice.”
 “Inbound international flights will be managed on a case by case basis,” the FAA said. 
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was “no indication as of yet” that there was anything “nefarious” that caused the ground stop. He said it was the result of a telecommunications outage “as of now.”
 Mullin said they are “are not ruling out anything at this point” in terms of what caused the communications issue. He said those currently on flights have no reason for concern. 
 “We are assured that everybody is safe,” he said, adding that it was unprecedented.
 “FAA technicians are investigating the issue,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in an online post. “We will provide immediate updates as we have them.”
 Shortly before the FAA issued its alert, both major airports in Chicago — O’Hare International Airport and Midway International Airport — were listed on a ground stop alert due to an “equipment outage,” NBC Chicago reported.

 Slide 1 of 1 Deveren Werne was on an American Airlines jet that was about to take off from Indianapolis to Chicago when suddenly the pilots announced that all flights were grounded.
 “At first the pilot announced that there was some kind of radio issue,” Werne, 55, of Greenville, South Carolina, told NBC News in a telephone interview. “Then a little while later, the pilot said something like, ‘There is something going on that’s more serious than that.’”

 Slide 1 of 1 Werne, a consultant who helps manufacturers and other industries adapt AI technology, said he is a frequent flyer and this was a first for him. He said there was “a mixture of emotions” from his fellow passengers on hearing the announcement.
 “Then I started hearing from other friends who were on planes, including one in Chicago who was stuck on a runway,” Werne said. “Right now our plane is heading back to the terminal so at least we’re going to be able to deplane.”
 At Newark Liberty International Airport, personnel in the control tower said the situation is “a whole mess right now,” according to LiveATC. “We’re running out of space” and “there’s significant gate issues” were comments also heard on the live audio feed. 
 “I’m as much in the dark as everyone else, I’m not getting any information from anybody,” one controller at Newark said, according to the feed.
 United Airlines issued a statement acknowledging the ground stop. “United flights that are already airborne will continue,” the statement said. “New domestic flights will not depart while the FAA ground stop remains in place.”
 Nationwide ground stops are extremely rare. 
 After the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, the FAA ordered an unprecedented nationwide ground stop. All civilian air traffic across U.S. airspace was halted and airborne planes were ordered to land at the nearest available airports.
 In January 2023, the FAA grounded all flights, blaming a failure in the Notice to Air Missions system, which alerts pilots to a host of potential dangers.
